Before submitting your remix, check that you've followed all the rules, and make adjustments if necessary:
Only @Burgnew_On_A_Laptop, @ZYellow, @Kyle3912Again, @SCRACO65, @Eliminated, @BobbyTheCatTheFirst, @SlyCotton-Apriwolf and @meow10010 are allowed to break these rules.
Rules marked with a (!) can ONLY be broken by @Burgnew_On_A_Laptop, nobody else!
(!) 1. Remember REMIX ETIQUETTE: Comment "Remixing..." in the comments before starting a remix so people know not to accidentally split the remix tree's branches. If you don't intend to make a new remix branch, then don't remix if someone has commented "Remixing...".
(!) 2. DO NOT BREAK SCRATCH'S COMMUNITY GUIDELINES (SCG), so nothing too scary, gory or vulgar!!
(!) 3. Don't add or remove anyone from the breaking rules list without permission. Furthermore, don't delete any of these rules or instructions & don't completely change the project title either.
4. Don't delete or ruin anything you didn't make, unless to fix glitches, errors or rule-breaks, delete unused scripts, or (only if you're a rule-breaker) to add a new feature to the game.
5. Don't make your characters too large, that would make it hard to see or make them too inaccurate compared to their hitbox. I suggest scaling your character assets IN THE COSTUME EDITOR to match the size of the other characters before making your other costumes.
6. I don't recommend adding any singular characters that appear to be 2 separate characters (EG: Mario & Luigi both as 1 player), unless they are stuck together with no feasible way to physically detach them.
7. Don't delete any music tracks unless they break the SCG. If you don't want to listen to a certain song or genre, utilize the "audio exemption" functionality to make sure you can't.
9. On the topic of music, please also refer to the Music comment's recommended music limit so this project's file size doesn't bloat too quickly.
10. You can add yourself to the thumbnail, but please don't delete any characters off it (unless they must be removed due to breaking the rules) or completely change it altogether.
11. If you are part of the "breaking rules" list, you're allowed to add a new rule if needed. Remember to add it to both the RULE RECAP comment and the project's instructions!

Barrel Castle - List of Barrel Types
This is a list of all the objects - barrel or not - that may be dispensed out of the barrel cannon in 'AY Climbing Barrel Castle!'. Most barrel types will squish climbers flat while they're flat-footed, and bump them backwards when they're airborne.

BARREL (brown): Just an ordinary wooden barrel, and the most common type to appear.

LIGHT BARREL (periwinkle): Rolls faster & falls slower than the other barrels.

HEAVY BARREL (salmon): Rolls slower & falls faster than the other barrels.

SPIKED BARREL (maroon): KOs players & forces them to respawn back at the bottom of the castle, so you'd better be careful around them! The spiked wall behind the starting line acts the same way.

PAUSE BARREL (dark green): The pause potions inside will pause climbers it hits in place for 5 seconds, or until they're hit by another barrel. An exception is made for already-paused climbers; they'll be unpaused & bumped/squished like they were hit by a regular barrel.

BOUNCY BARREL (magenta): Bounces across the platforms as it traverses the arena. It's specific movement style depends on if it's a 'Rolling Bouncy Barrel', or 'Falling Bouncy Barrel'...

Rolling Bouncy Barrels bounce across the platforms just like other barrels would roll, without stopping to fall down ladders.
Falling Bouncy Barrels bound upon every platform once as they tumble straight to the bottom, steering left or right with every bounce.

TRANSFORMER BARREL: (salmon-lavender gradient): The barrel potions inside will transform climbers it hits into a barrel (without limbs, unlike the Barrel Squad members), causing them to tumble backwards about the length of one platform.

WARPING BARREL (purple): The warp potions inside will teleport any climbers it hits to a random location on one of the platforms - it can be either helpful or hindering, depending on where it sends them.

TNT BARREL (sunglow): The first climber to run into this explosive barrel will cause it to detonate & go BOOM, KOing them & blasting backwards anyone else caught in range of the explosion!

TAR BARREL (black): Leaks sticky tar behind it as it rolls, slowing down other climbers & barrels traversing it. The tar starts drying up after about 15 seconds. It also falls slightly faster than all other barrels except for the Heavy Barrel.

RAINBOW STAR (rainbow): The RAREST object to ever dispense from a barrel cannon, even if it's NOT a barrel! Bouncing along the platforms like a Rolling Bouncy Barrel, the first player to collect it will become completely INVINCIBLE for about 7.5 seconds, being completely unaffected by any other barrel, not even being slowed by spilled tar! In addition, they'll move slightly faster & knock back any other climbers they ram through! All these abilities make this the must-have item for higher-end difficulties.

This AY-minigame is the first to introduce multiple Delight/Dismay reactions and custom footstep sets!

Change all the "voice" sound clips to your own character's voice - if they don't have one, either mute the voiceclips, or make them into some of the character's non-vocal sounds if they have any.
You're also free to change the Footstep and Jump sounds to your own preferences if you'd wish - just make sure the amount of footsteps you add matches the amount in the above custom block. 

VOICE-CLIP GUIDE:
OUCH: A pained grunt or yelp usually made when hit by a barrel or other hazard. You can add as many as you want (around 3-5 recommended), but remember to set their amount in the custom block.

DELIGHT: A positive reaction to an event! Usually plays in tandem with the corresponding costume. You can add as many as you want (around 2-3 recommended), but remember to set their amount in the custom block.

DISMAY: A negative reaction to an event. Usually players in tandem with the corresponding costume. You can add as many as you want (around 2-3 recommended), but remember to set their amount in the custom block.

KO!: Screaming and shouting while falling off the castle after being knocked out by a hazard, usually a Spiked Barrel!

WIN!: The character's triumphant victory phrase for whenever they reach the goal!

If you want to add your own music loops...
1) Separate your song into it's intro (if it has an intro) and the section that loops. (if you're looping a music track that originally doesn't loop, you may also save the end section in it's own sound for another time)
2) Tag '-Start' at the end of the intro's name, and tag '-Loop' onto the looping part's name too.
3) Add the song's name into the 'Add music' block that matches which scenario it's for, and drop it here. 
Remember that the song name must always be spelt the same, or else the loop won't work! If you're unsure, test it.

If the music track comes from a party game, like Mario Party, Wii Party or WarioWare: MEGA Party Game$, make sure it won't play for users who don't want those music tracks, like SmashBrosFan2020, via the audio-exemption lists & booleans. Same goes for "gets faster" tracks, lyrical music, Flash/HTML5 game music, Miitopia music, Friday Night Funkin' music & non-looping music. 
Burgnew recommends you refrain from adding more than around 100 music tracks total, so that lower-level devices aren't overwhelmed by assets while trying to load or save the project. You should also refrain from adding too many music tracks longer than 200 seconds total or too many "gets faster" tracks.
